title: The King Who Tried to Sweep the Sand (TA)
summary: Akbar becomes obsessed with clearing a sand dune that continually blows onto the highway. Birbal shows him the folly of fighting nature with brooms.
full_text:
A strong desert wind blew across the western border of the empire, constantly depositing a large dune of loose red sand across a vital military highway. Emperor Akbar ordered two hundred laborers with brooms and shovels to clear the sand.

For three weeks, the laborers swept and shoveled from dawn till dusk. But every afternoon, the desert wind blew again, depositing twice as much sand across the road!

Frustrated, Akbar rode to the site and shouted: 'Bring five hundred more men! Double the brooms! I will conquer this sand!'

Birbal, who had accompanied the Emperor, walked to the edge of the dunes, picked up a handful of dry sand, and let it slip through his fingers into the wind.

Birbal asked: 'Sire, what are you trying to accomplish?'

Akbar seethed: 'I am clearing this road! The desert must obey the Emperor!'

Birbal smiled gently:

'Your Majesty, you are trying to conquer the ocean of the desert with a broom! As long as the wind blows across a thousand miles of sand, shovels can accomplish nothing.

'Man cannot defeat nature by stubborn brute force; he must work with nature's laws.'

Birbal brought the local desert nomad elders and asked their advice.

The nomads advised: 'Plant rows of hardy desert tamarisk bushes, thorny acacia trees, and deep-rooted camel grass along the northern ridge fifty paces from the road. The roots will bind the soil, and the dense thorny hedge will break the wind, causing the sand to drop before it ever reaches the highway.'

Akbar followed the advice. Within six months, the green hedge grew, trapping the drifting sand harmlessly on the dunes, leaving the roadway completely clear and open!

Birbal said to the Emperor:

'You see, Sire? Two hundred brooms could not clear the road for three weeks, but a hedge of humble desert grass solved the problem for a century!

'In governance, do not exhaust your treasury trying to sweep away social problems with harsh force. Plant the living hedges of education, justice, and opportunity, and the winds of discord will drop their burdens harmlessly outside your gates.'

Akbar took the lesson to heart, praising Birbal for replacing brute labor with environmental wisdom.
moral: நீதி மற்றும் வாழ்க்கை பாடம்: Wit beats power
